fact: The AACP Level of Care Utilization System, Adult Version 20 (December 2016), rates patients on six dimensions: risk of harm, functional status, medical/addictive/psychiatric comorbidity, recovery environment, treatment and recovery history, and engagement and recovery status. The scores map to six levels of care running from recovery maintenance and health management up to medically managed residential services.
source_title: LOCUS (AACP) Instrument Version Twenty, public version (LA County DMH copy)

fact: The AACP child and adolescent tool, CALOCUS Version 20 (July 2019), also uses six dimensions, with comorbidity including developmental problems and the last two dimensions framed as resiliency/treatment history and treatment acceptance/engagement. It lists basic services plus levels one to six, from recovery maintenance to the most intensive medically monitored residence-based care. The page read did not mention CASII or an age range.
source_title: CALOCUS Child and Adolescent Version 20 (AACP instrument, vendor-hosted copy)

fact: Volume 1 of the fourth edition of The ASAM Criteria became available digitally on 5 October 2023. It adds a level 1.0 for monitoring patients in stable remission, folds withdrawal management and biomedical services into the continuum, builds co-occurring-capable care into core standards at every level, and stresses recovery support and harm reduction.
source_title: ASAM news: Crucial changes to substance use and co-occurring disorder care standards published

fact: DEA and HHS issued a fourth temporary extension of the COVID-era flexibilities, announced 31 December 2025, running through 31 December 2026. During this time DEA-registered practitioners may prescribe controlled medications by telemedicine without a prior in-person evaluation, if federal and state requirements are otherwise met. The release did not discuss the special registration rule. Status after 2026 should be rechecked.
source_title: DEA press release: DEA Extends Telemedicine Flexibilities to Ensure Continued Access to Care

topic: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and crisis care
fact: The 988 Lifeline (phone, chat, text; free, confidential, 24/7) is run under SAMHSA. The July 16, 2022 launch date, the Vibrant administrator role and the 'someone to call, someone to respond, somewhere to go' framing are from search snippets only; the SAMHSA timeline body did not load and the 988 pages were blocked.

topic: Philippine Mental Health Act (RA 11036): consent and involuntary treatment
fact: RA 11036, approved 20 June 2018, requires written informed consent before treatment and presumes every person has legal capacity (Sec. 8). Treatment, restraint or confinement without consent is limited to psychiatric or neurologic emergencies or impaired decision-making capacity, must follow advance directives where safe, and needs an attending professional's order reviewed by the internal review board within 15 days and every 15 days thereafter (Sec. 13). Failure to obtain consent outside those exceptions is penalized (Sec. 44).
source_title: Republic Act No. 11036 (Mental Health Act), Philippine Judiciary E-Library

topic: Philippine Mental Health Act (RA 11036): confidentiality and records
fact: Sec. 5(l) bars disclosure of a service user's information and records without written consent, except when required by law or court order, with consent, to prevent harm in a life-threatening emergency, in suspected child abuse, or in proceedings against a professional for negligence or ethics breaches. Users can access their own records (Sec. 5(r)), though access may be withheld if it would cause harm, subject to challenge. Breach of confidentiality carries penalties (Sec. 44(b)).
source_title: Republic Act No. 11036 (Mental Health Act), Philippine Judiciary E-Library

topic: APA Opinions of the Ethics Committee, 2025 edition; Principles edition
fact: The APA published the 2025 edition of the Opinions of the Ethics Committee on the Principles of Medical Ethics. Its foreword identifies the 2013 edition of the Principles With Annotations Especially Applicable to Psychiatry as the version officially adopted and binding on members.
source_title: Opinions of the Ethics Committee on the Principles of Medical Ethics, 2025 edition (APA)

topic: Sex with current and former patients (APA)
fact: The APA Opinions state that the ethical prohibition on romantic entanglements with patients is absolute (Opinion A.25), and that a dating or social relationship with a former patient would be exploitative and unethical (Opinion A.8). The AMA position was not checked.
source_title: Opinions of the Ethics Committee on the Principles of Medical Ethics, 2025 edition (APA)

fact: Section 7.3 was adopted in 1973 after a 1964 magazine survey in which psychiatrists diagnosed a presidential candidate they had not examined. It allows sharing general psychiatric expertise but deems it unethical to give a professional opinion about a person without an examination and proper authorization. The APA reaffirmed it in news releases dated 16 March and 6 October 2017.

topic: ACGME duty hours, 2017 Common Program Requirements
fact: Effective 1 July 2017, first-year residents returned to the same limits as other residents: shifts up to 24 hours plus up to 4 hours for care transitions, replacing the 16-hour cap set in 2011. The 80-hour weekly limit averaged over four weeks, one day off in seven, and in-house call no more often than every third night remain. Specialties may set stricter limits.
source_title: ACGME releases revised Common Program Requirements, Section VI (newsroom, March 2017)

topic: HIPAA: serious and imminent threat and psychotherapy notes
fact: HIPAA permits a provider to disclose protected information, including psychotherapy notes, when it reasonably believes this is needed to prevent a serious and imminent threat, to someone able to lessen it, consistent with state law and ethics. Psychotherapy notes kept separate from the record otherwise generally need patient authorization. Capable adults who object limit disclosure to family unless that threat standard is met. This relates to Tarasoff-type duties, which vary by state.
source_title: HHS OCR: HIPAA FAQ on disclosure if a patient is a danger; HHS guidance on HIPAA and sharing mental health information (publication date not stated on page)

topic: FSMB Policy on Physician Illness and Impairment
fact: The FSMB House of Delegates adopted this policy in April 2021. It says illness alone is not impairment, which is a functional inability to practice with reasonable skill and safety. It urges boards not to require disclosure of treatment through physician health programs and to drop licensing questions about current conditions or counseling, to reduce stigma.
source_title: FSMB: Policy on Physician Illness and Impairment: Towards a Model that Optimizes Patient Safety and Physician Health

topic: Dr. Lorna Breen Health Care Provider Protection Act
fact: Signed 18 March 2022, the Act funds education and awareness efforts and training to support the mental health of health care workers, including residents, with up to $135 million over three years. Only a university news page was read, not the statute or a federal source.
source_title: Columbia University Irving Medical Center news: Dr. Lorna Breen Health Care Provider Protection Act Signed Into Law

topic: WHO/OHCHR guidance on mental health, human rights and legislation
fact: Launched 9 October 2023, the guidance helps countries reform laws to end coercive practices such as involuntary detention, forced treatment, seclusion and restraint, with free and informed consent as the basis of all interventions. It urges replacing institutions with community support, includes a checklist for reviewing laws against international human rights obligations, and stresses involving people with lived experience.
source_title: WHO news: WHO, OHCHR launch new guidance to improve laws addressing human rights abuses in mental health care
